Rationale.CS1_Results_vs_Conclusion: All major conclusions are directly supported by explicit quantitative results. The paper claims: (1) FVs exist as compact task representations - supported by Table 2 showing 39.1%->90.8% (shuffled) and 5.5%->57.5% (zero-shot) accuracy improvements for GPT-J; (2) FVs are portable across contexts - supported by Table 3 showing natural text improvements from ~0-2.7% to 46-67.7%; (3) FVs are distinct from word embeddings - supported by Table 6 showing reconstructed FVs cannot recover full performance; (4) FVs can be composed - supported by Table 7 showing composition results. No conclusions contradict or exaggerate the documented results.
Rationale.CS2_Plan_vs_Implementation: The documentation describes a clear methodology in Section 2: (1) extract average activations from ICL prompts (Section 2.1), (2) formulate attention head outputs (Section 2.2), (3) apply causal mediation analysis to identify causal heads using AIE (Section 2.3, Equations 2-4), (4) sum attention head outputs to form FV (Equation 5), (5) test FV by adding to hidden states. Section 3 experiments follow this methodology precisely. Appendix C provides detailed experimental parameters: 100 clean prompts for FV extraction, 25 corrupted prompts for AIE, 10 attention heads for GPT-J, evaluation at layer |L|/3.
Rationale.CS3_Effect_Size: Effect sizes are clearly non-trivial and large relative to baselines. Zero-shot: GPT-J improves from 5.5% to 57.5% (+52 pp), Llama 2 (70B) from 8.2% to 83.8% (+75.6 pp). Shuffled-label: GPT-J from 39.1% to 90.8% (+51.7 pp). FV (57.5%) vastly outperforms layer average baseline (9.5%) in zero-shot. Natural text portability shows +43 to +67 pp improvements. These represent multiplicative improvements (10x in some cases) over baselines, not marginal effects.
Rationale.CS4_Justification: Key design choices are explicitly justified: (1) Causal mediation analysis chosen 'to distill the information flow during ICL' with references to Pearl (2001), Vig et al. (2020), Meng et al. (2022); (2) Focus on attention heads because 'those are the components used by transformer LMs to move information between different token positions'; (3) 10 attention heads chosen because 'the increase in performance begins to plateau when using |A|=10' (Figure 6); (4) Layer |L|/3 chosen based on empirical results 'which we found works well in practice' with Figure 4 showing layer-wise patterns.
Rationale.CS5_Statistical_Significance: Key results report uncertainty with standard deviations over 5 random seeds, as explicitly stated: 'all accuracies and standard deviations over 5 random seeds' (Section 3.1). Table 2: 90.8+/-0.9%, 57.5+/-1.7%. Table 3: natural text results with +/-3.8%, +/-3.0% etc. Table 6: reconstruction comparisons include +/-. Table 7: composition results like 0.25+/-0.02. The methodology for computing uncertainty is clearly explained.
